title: Plaice weight-length coefficient peaks near the size of sexual maturity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Plaice weight-length coefficient peaks near the size of sexual maturity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In plaice the weight-length coefficient k = W/L^3 is not constant but rises to a maximum and then slowly declines with increasing size, the maximum falling near 30 cm, about the size at which sexual maturity begins.

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: k = W/L^3 not constant in plaice; \max_L k at L \approx 30\,\text{cm}

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we see that _k_ is by no means constant, but steadily increases to a maximum, and afterwards slowly declines with the increasing size of the fish

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Weight-length coefficient in fish”. Scope: plaice (and by extension other fishes)

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: k = W/L^3 not constant in plaice; \max_L k at L \approx 30\,\text{cm}

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-17: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.86

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The taxon, equation, curve shape and approximate peak are explicit. Large public fisheries records permit a rapid stratified test with sufficient size coverage and independent maturity information.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For plaice records, calculate k = W/L^3, model it flexibly against length, and locate its maximum relative to independently measured maturity size. Constant or monotonic k, or a peak far from approximately 30 cm and maturity onset, would refute the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some survey records lack individual weight or maturity.

Sex, season and stock alter condition and maturity size.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Individual length, weight, and maturity for plaice are in a long-running open trawl-survey database, so k against length and the maturity comparison are routine. The predicted hump is specific enough to fail. Stock differences and season can move the peak, and those factors can be stratified in the same data rather than left as an uncontrolled confound. The extension to other fishes is extra; the plaice claim itself is resolvable now.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For plaice, compute k = W/L^3 by length bin and compare the length of the maximum with the length at which maturity begins. A rise to a maximum and a later slow decline, with that maximum near 30 cm and near the maturity ogive, would support the claim. A flat k, or a maximum far from maturity, would refute the stated pattern.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Seasonal condition and gear selectivity can shift the apparent maximum.

The 30 cm figure belongs to the stocks Thompson knew; other plaice stocks may mature at another length.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In North Sea plaice sampled in late winter, the weight-length coefficient k = W/L^3 averaged by length class rises with length to a maximum near 30 cm, close to the length at which sexual maturity begins, and then declines slowly at larger sizes.

fields.label: Method
fields.value: Downloaded eight NS-IBTS CA XML files from the DATRAS web service, kept Pleuronectes platessa records (Aphia 127143; Q1 2015-2019: 12504 records, Q3 2017-2019: 9514), converted mm length classes to cm, and computed k = 10,000 W/L^3 per fish (11474 Q1 fish of 15-50 cm with weight). Class means of k by 1-cm length class (>= 30 fish) were smoothed with a 3-class running mean and the maximum located; the same was done by sex, by year and for Q3. Maturity codes were mapped to immature (…1) / mature (…2-5) and a maximum-likelihood logistic ogive gave L50 pooled and by sex (10464 Q1 fish with maturity codes).

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered. Data: ICES DATRAS exchange-format CA (age/biology) records for the North Sea IBTS, quarter 1 (January-February, the closest survey season to Thompson's March 1907 sample), years 2015-2019, species Pleuronectes platessa (Aphia 127143), individual weight > 0, lengths converted to cm. Compute k = 1000 W/L^3 (W in g, L in cm) per fish, average by 1-cm length class over 15-50 cm keeping classes with >= 30 fish, smooth with a 3-class running mean, and let L* be the length of the maximum smoothed k. Maturity: from the same Q1 CA records with a maturity code, classify immature (scale code ending in 1) vs mature (codes ending 2-5), fit a logistic of maturity on length (sexes pooled; by sex reported) and take L50. Supports if all hold: (1) hump: L* is at least 3 cm above the smallest and 3 cm below the largest analysed class, and smoothed k(L*) exceeds smoothed k at both ends of the analysed range by >= 3%; (2) 25 <= L* <= 35 cm; (3) |L* - L50| <= 5 cm. Secondary (reported): the same by sex, and for quarter 3 (2017-2019).

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Refutes if smoothed k is flat (max - min over classes < 3% of the mean) or monotonic (maximum at an end of the analysed range), or if L* lies outside 22-38 cm. Mixed if a hump exists in the right place but is more than 5 cm from L50, or if the hump exists only in one sex or season.

fields.label: Unit
fields.value: cm, length class of maximum smoothed k in Q1 (upper end of analysed range 16-43 cm); k x 10^4 falls from 97.9 at 16 cm to a minimum of 93.1 at 26-27 cm and rises to 100.2 at 43 cm

fields.label: Uncertainty
fields.value: class means based on 36-646 fish per class; standard deviations in derived/k_by_length.csv; the same U-shape appears in each year, each sex and in Q3

fields.label: Interpretation
fields.value: Thompson's k is the Fulton condition factor computed by length class from mean weights of trawl-caught plaice 'in a particular locality and at a particular time'. Modern survey fish are weighed individually, so class means of individual k are used, which is equivalent for the purpose. 'Near 30 cm' is read as 25-35 cm; 'about the size at which sexual maturity begins' is read as within 5 cm of the length at 50% maturity in the same samples, since the onset of maturity is not sharply defined. North Sea plaice today mature at smaller sizes than in 1907, so criterion (3) tests the coupling to maturity rather than the fixed 30 cm figure, while (2) tests the figure itself.

fields.label: Datasets
fields.value:
ICES DATRAS exchange data, CA records, North Sea IBTS quarter 1, 2015-2019

ICES DATRAS exchange data, CA records, North Sea IBTS quarter 3, 2017-2019

fields.label: Caveats
fields.value:
The modern pattern is the inverse of Thompson's: k is highest in the smallest fish, falls to a minimum at 24-28 cm and rises again toward 40+ cm (a U, not a hump), in Q1 pooled, in each year 2015-2019, in each sex, and in Q3 (minimum 25-27 cm). No class near 30 cm is a maximum.

Scope difference: Thompson's 1907 fish came from 'a particular locality' in March with k from class mean weights; here fish are pooled across the whole North Sea survey and weighed individually. Spatial pooling can blur a local hump but cannot manufacture a minimum, and the by-year and by-sex replicates agree.

Maturity has shifted: North Sea plaice now reach 50% maturity at ~18 cm pooled (females 22.5 cm, males 15.2 cm) in Q1, far below the ~30 cm Thompson cited, so criterion (3) could not have been met at 30 cm even if a hump existed there. The k minimum (~26 cm) lies near the female L50, the opposite sign of the association Thompson proposed.

Notation: the pre-registration wrote k = 1000 W/L^3; the analysis reports k x 10^4 as Thompson did (plaice k ~ 100). The scaling does not affect any criterion.

Q3 maturity codes are sparse (1,652 fish) and Q3 L50 (~25 cm) differs from Q1; Q1 is the pre-registered primary season.

fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth
